![](images/icon.svg){height=139px fig-alt="metadata-mender hex logo"}

## What it is

**Metadata Mender** is a Zotero 9–10.0 plugin that takes the items you already
have and *mends* them: it looks up each item's DOI, PMID, or CRAN package
id against eight free databases and fills in the gaps — title, journal,
volume/issue/pages, ISSN, authors, abstract, URL, publisher — while also
recording the current citation count, an OpenAlex 2-year mean citedness, and the open-access PDF link when one exists.

It is not a search tool. It assumes you already curate your library in
Zotero and simply want the metadata to be *complete and correct*.

## Install

**Declared compatibility:** Zotero 9.0 through 10.0.x. Current qualification
and limitations are recorded in [the audit](AUDIT-2026-10-30.md).

1. Download the latest `metadata-mender-<version>.xpi` from the
   [Releases page](https://github.com/CTTIR/metadata-mender/releases).
2. In Zotero open **Tools → Plugins**, click the gear icon, and choose
   **Install Plugin From File…**.
3. Select the `.xpi` and restart Zotero if prompted.


## Set up your contact email

Open **Zotero → Settings → Metadata Mender** and enter a contact email.
This single field unlocks the polite-pool throughput at Crossref and is
the required identifier for Unpaywall. Everything else (API keys for
OpenAlex, NCBI, Semantic Scholar, CORE, Crossref Plus) is optional and
controls service access and throughput; CORE requests require its key.


## A typical run

1. Select one or more regular items in your library (notes and
   attachments are ignored).
2. Right-click and choose **Mend metadata (DOI/PMID lookup)**.
3. A progress popup ticks per item. Press **Esc** at any time to stop
   pending work. A save already underway may finish.

For each item the plugin:

- Reads the DOI (from the DOI field or the `Extra` field) and PMID
  (from `Extra`).
- Queries the configured sources in priority order. The first source
  with a non-empty value for a given field wins.
- If neither a DOI nor a PMID is present, optionally falls back to a
  Crossref title search, **off by default**. A match requires one distinct DOI,
  title similarity ≥ 0.92, matching first-author surname, publication title and
  type, and a publication year within one year. Missing evidence means no match.
- Writes provenance, citation count, OpenAlex mean citedness, and any
  open-access PDF link back to `Extra`.
- Tags changed items with `mended:YYYY-MM-DD` (or a stable `mended`
  tag, per your tag policy).


## What gets written

Stable identifiers are appended once; temporal data (citations, mean
citedness, OA link) is rewritten on every run with today's date so the
series stays comparable across runs.

| Line | Behaviour | Source |
|------|-----------|--------|
| `PMID: <id>` | Append once | PubMed / Semantic Scholar |
| `PMCID: PMC<id>` | Append once | OpenAlex / PubMed / Semantic Scholar |
| `arXiv: <id>` | Append once | Semantic Scholar |
| `OpenAlex: W<id>` | Append once | OpenAlex |
| `Citations: <n> [<source>, YYYY-MM-DD]` | Rewritten every run | OpenAlex (preferred) → Crossref → Semantic Scholar |
| `OpenAlex 2yr mean citedness: <x.xx> [OpenAlex 2yr mean citedness, YYYY-MM-DD]` | Rewritten every run | OpenAlex venue lookup |
| `OA-URL: <url>` | Rewritten every run | OpenAlex → Unpaywall → OpenAIRE → CORE |
| `Provenance: YYYY-MM-DD — field:source, …` | Rewritten on any change | derived from the merges actually performed |

## R packages

To mend a software item that represents an R package, give it either:

- a URL of the form `https://cran.r-project.org/package=ggplot2` in the
  Zotero **URL** field, or
- a line `CRAN: ggplot2` in **Extra**.

The plugin queries METACRAN (`crandb.r-pkg.org`) and fills in the
package title, abstract, version, date, language ("R"), publisher
("CRAN"), authors (with `[role]` and ORCID annotations stripped), and
URL, plus `License:`, `Upstream-URL:`, and `CRAN:` lines.

## Reading the run summary

```
Done. N updated, N unchanged, N skipped, N not found, N errored.
```

- **updated** — at least one field or `Extra` line changed; a
  `mended:YYYY-MM-DD` tag was added.
- **unchanged** — sources answered but had nothing new.
- **skipped** — item has no DOI/PMID and the title fallback is off or
  did not produce a confident match.
- **not found** — every source returned 404.
- **errored** — no verified metadata was available, identity checks failed, or a save failed.
- Protected, trashed, pending-edit, or changed-during-lookup items are skipped.
  Partial source failures are also reported when another source succeeds.

Per-item errors are surfaced inline (up to five) in the progress popup;
sanitized failure details appear in **Help → Debug Output**.

## Tips

- Start with **Fill empty fields only** mode for your first run, then
  spot-check before switching to **Overwrite existing fields**.
- OpenAlex 2-year mean citedness is a distinct metric, not the Clarivate JIF.
  Existing manual or legacy `Impact Factor:` lines are preserved.
- Existing settings are preserved during upgrades; check Update mode. New
  installations default to fill mode, full names, and no title search.
- Selected identifiers leave the machine for metadata lookup. Optional title
  search sends the title and first author to Crossref.
- Zotero HTTP debug logs may include lookup identifiers, titles and contact
  email; review logs before sharing them. Plugin error messages omit request URLs.
- Run Mender before Workbench extraction/audit, close Zotero for Workbench
  operations, and regenerate correction plans after library changes.
- Author name parsing for PubMed's "Surname IN" form is heuristic;
  spot-check authors after a bulk overwrite run.

## Build from source

With Python 3.9+ and Node.js 22+, from the repository root:

```bash
node --test tests/*.test.js
./build.sh
python3 tools/build.py --check metadata-mender-0.6.1.xpi
```

Builds reproducibly, verifies runtime bytes against source, and preserves
older artifacts. Install the local XPI and first use a disposable reference
with **Fill empty fields only** selected. Automated tests use stubs and do
not prove desktop UI or external-service availability.
